title: token_compression_layer
goal: reduce model-visible context through typed semantic and structural reduction while preserving task-critical evidence
completion_evidence: reducer metadata, test-output recall, diff recall, and budget-aware section assembly are covered by focused Rust tests
normal command capture and public telemetry remain unchanged until runtime wiring is explicit
constraints: optimize effective input tokens, not compressed byte count
preserve schema, policy, quarantine, replay, and telemetry contracts
keep lossy reduction explicit and recoverable
prefer command-specific deterministic reducers over generic salience ranking
do not use hash-only schema or context references unless expansion is guaranteed
keep assembly and SIMD out of capture/control-plane token compression
consensus: semantic and structural reduction is the primary prompt-token optimization path
typed metadata should start internal and compact before any public artifact contract
critical-span recall gates are required before broad reducer rollout
byte compression is useful for storage and replay artifacts, not model-visible prompt text
Rust library and allocation improvements come before any low-level optimization

slices.goal: capture the Phase X design, reducer acceptance gates, fixture classes, and recall metrics
add private reducer metadata for kind, version, profile, stats, lossiness, uncertainty, and replay pointers without changing public output
implement the first command-specific reducer with recall gates for failing tests, panic/error/assertion blocks, final summaries, and exit status
add diff reducer recall gates for headers, hunk headers, changed lines, rename/binary markers, and touched paths
assemble compressed context by priority tiers with stable section ordering, omission records, and high-uncertainty fallback
